topic: The Pulse of Rhythm: An Introduction to Music and Measure Theory
target_audience: Middle school students or introductory music theory learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse
lecture_lines: Music starts with a steady, recurring pulse.
Think of a heartbeat, always consistent.
These pulses provide our musical foundation.
animations: Create a glowing dot in the center of the screen (#00FF00) to represent the 'Beat'. (Wait 4s)
Animate the dot pulsing in size (scale up and down) every 1 second to emulate a heartbeat. (Wait 4s)
Fade in a label below the dot reading 'Pulse' in white (#FFFFFF) to establish the conceptual tool. (Wait 4s)

sections.title: The Bar Line: Organizing the Chaos
lecture_lines: We group pulses into equal measures.
Vertical bar lines mark the separation.
These help organize rhythmic flow clearly.
animations: Render 12 dots arranged in a horizontal row (#FFFFFF) in Row B. (Wait 3s)
Animate a vertical line (#FF0000) drawing itself after every 4th dot to create the 'Bar Line'. (Wait 3s)
Animate the groups of 4 dots shifting slightly to define the 'Measures' clearly. (Wait 3s)

sections.title: Time Signature: The Mathematical Blueprint
lecture_lines: Time signatures act as our blueprint.
The top number sets beats per measure.
The bottom defines the beat's value.
Together they guide the rhythmic structure.
Imagine a chef filling musical bowls.
animations: Render a bowl shape (#FFFF00) as the 'Measure' in Row E. (Wait 3s)
Animate 4 distinct musical notes falling into the bowl one by one. (Wait 3s)
Animate a vertical wall appearing at the end of the 4th note to seal the bowl. (Wait 3s)
Add a label '4/4' above the bowl in Row D in cyan (#00FFFF) to represent the Time Signature. (Wait 3s)
Flash the label '4/4' three times to emphasize its role as the mathematical blueprint. (Wait 3s)

sections.title: Visualizing Fractions in Time
lecture_lines: Notes are like fractions of time.
Whole notes fill the entire measure.
Smaller notes divide the circle equally.
They sum perfectly to one measure.
Each wedge completes our musical clock.
animations: Render a circular clock (#FFFFFF) as a 'Whole Note' placeholder in Row B. (Wait 3s)
Animate two semi-circular wedges (#FF00FF) appearing to fill the clock face. (Wait 3s)
Animate the wedges fading into labels '1/2' in white to visualize the fractions. (Wait 3s)
Change the circle color to gradient red to green to show it filling over time. (Wait 3s)
Trigger a flash effect when the clock is full to indicate 'Measure Complete'. (Wait 3s)

sections.title: Application: The Marching Ants
lecture_lines: Marching ants show rhythm in action.
Every fourth ant wears a cap.
This accent creates a predictable structure.
The measure theory brings music order.
Rhythm is simply math in motion.
animations: Render 8 ants in a line in Row E, moving left to right across the screen (#FFA500). (Wait 3s)
Animate every 4th ant appearing with a blue cap (#0000FF) as they walk. (Wait 3s)
Animate the capped ants flashing brighter to emphasize the first beat accent. (Wait 3s)
